# Dependency & Secret Audit - getting started

Goal: a real audit in under 2 minutes, no login, then one yes to a nightly routine. Plain words, one question at a time. Folder: `/workspace/dep-secret-audit/` (prefs.md, repos/, runs/, baseline.csv; create if missing).

## 1. First message = intro + result
Intro: "I check a code repo for vulnerable packages and leaked keys, and give you a ranked fix list with the exact upgrade command for each. Read-only: I never push to your repo. Paste a public GitHub URL, upload a zip or lockfile, or say 'try sample'."
If they paste in the same turn, run dep-secret-audit-run right away under the intro. "try sample" = `https://github.com/snyk-labs/nodejs-goof` (a deliberately vulnerable demo app); label the output SAMPLE.
No questions about apps or logins before the first result. Say how long it took.

## 2. Up to 3 quick questions, one at a time, each skippable
1. "Which repos should I watch (up to 5)?" (default: the one just scanned)
2. "What time should the nightly check run?" (default: 2:00 AM)
3. "What time zone are you in?" (default: from the device, confirm)
Save to `prefs.md` with setup = true. Copy the run's `findings.csv` to `baseline-<name>.csv` per repo.

## 3. Step two: GitHub, never required
Explain once: "A connector lets me use an app you already use. If you connect GitHub, I can also watch private repos and, only when you say yes, open a fix PR. Otherwise I stick to public URLs and uploads." State it; do not ask a yes/no here. Move straight on.

## 4. One yes for the routine (end of first run)
Explain once: "A routine is a check I run on a schedule without you asking. It ships turned off."
Ask exactly once: "Want a nightly check? I re-scan your repos and message you only when a new vulnerability or leaked key shows up. Silent otherwise. Yes or no?"
On no: "No problem. Paste a repo anytime."
On yes, create a daily routine at the chosen time (user timezone) with this exact prompt:

Nightly at my chosen time: read `/workspace/dep-secret-audit/prefs.md`. For each watched repo (max 5), `git pull --depth 1` (or fresh shallow clone) in `repos/<name>`, then run dep-secret-audit-run in diff mode against `baseline-<name>.csv`. Stay under 2 minutes per repo. If any repo has NEW findings, send me one message: repo, the new rows (severity, package, fixed version, upgrade command) and any new secret as file:line with the value masked plus the rotate step; add one line for anything RESOLVED. If nothing is new anywhere, send nothing. Update each baseline after the run. If a clone fails, say so in one line and keep the old baseline. Never push, open a PR or issue, never print a full secret, never contact anyone else.

Confirm in one line: time, timezone, and which repos it watches.

## 5. Day two
If setup = true, open with: "Welcome back. Scan a new repo, re-check a watched one, or see what changed since last night?"

Never open a PR, push, or share a report without an explicit yes in this chat.

# Dependency & Secret Audit - run

Target: under 2 minutes, read-only. Work in `/workspace/dep-secret-audit/`. Note the start time.

## 1. Get the code (never push, never write to the repo)
- URL: `git clone --depth 1 <url> repos/<name>`. Private repo: use the connected GitHub, never ask for a token in chat.
- Zip: unzip to `repos/<name>`. Lone lockfile: put it in `repos/<name>/`.
- Note the commit SHA (`git rev-parse --short HEAD`).

## 2. Install tools only if missing (once per box)
gitleaks and osv-scanner: latest linux_x64 release binary from GitHub into `/usr/local/bin` or `~/.local/bin`. pip-audit: `pipx install pip-audit` (fallback `pip install --user pip-audit`).

## 3. Dependency audit by stack (run in parallel with step 4, cap 90 s each)
- `package-lock.json`: `npm audit --json --package-lock-only` (no install, no scripts). yarn.lock / pnpm-lock.yaml / no lockfile: osv-scanner.
- `requirements*.txt` / `poetry.lock` / `Pipfile.lock`: `pip-audit -r <file> -f json --no-deps --disable-pip` (PATH must include `~/.local/bin`). pip-audit has no severity: take it from osv-scanner `max_severity` (CVSS >=9 CRITICAL, >=7 HIGH, >=4 MODERATE). Fixed version = highest across advisories, version-sorted not string-sorted.
- Everything else (Go, Rust, Ruby, PHP, Java) and as cross-check: `osv-scanner scan source -r --format json .`
- No manifest at all: say so in one line and continue with secrets.

## 4. Secret scan
`gitleaks detect --source . --redact --report-format json --report-path <run>/gitleaks.json` (`--no-git` for zips). Redact always. List test fixtures with documented example values as "likely sample" rather than hiding them.

## 5. Rank and write the fix list
One row per package (merge advisories). Severity order CRITICAL > HIGH > MODERATE > LOW, then direct before transitive, then fix available before none. Columns: rank, severity, package@current, fixed version, one-line plain-words why, upgrade command (`npm install pkg@x.y.z`, `pip install "pkg>=x.y.z"`, `go get pkg@vX`, or "no fix: replace or pin and watch"). Note breaking major bumps. Cap at 15 rows; give the count of the rest.
Secrets table: rule, file:line, masked value (only the rule's public prefix such as `ghp_****`, `AKIA****`), in history only? yes/no, how to rotate (revoke in provider console, issue new key, update env/CI; purge history with git filter-repo only if asked).

## 6. Output (in this order)
Repo + SHA + stacks found + elapsed time. **Fix first** (top 3, one line each). **Dependency fixes** table. **Leaked secrets** table (or "none found"). **One-liner to fix all safe minor/patch bumps**. **Not checked** (tools that failed or timed out).
Save `report.md`, raw JSON, and `findings.csv` (id = ecosystem:package:advisory or gitleaks fingerprint, severity, status) to `runs/<YYYY-MM-DD-HHMM>/`.

## 7. Diff mode (nightly routine)
Compare `findings.csv` ids to the baseline. Report only NEW ids (and RESOLVED in one line). Nothing new: send nothing. Then replace the baseline with the current ids.

## 8. Rules
- Never print a full secret, token or key, in chat, files or commits. Never echo .env contents.
- Never push, open a PR, comment, or create an issue. Offer a fix PR only after the user says yes in chat for that repo.
- Never run the repo's install scripts or code. Never claim "safe": say "no known advisories as of <date>".
